title: Notification preferences and quiet hours
goal: Per-user notification preferences (channels by category, quiet hours) with GET/PUT endpoints and a pure evaluator the dispatcher uses to decide whether a push or os notification is suppressed.
scope_in: GET and PUT /v1/notification-preferences (PUT replaces the whole document).
Preference document validation: known categories only, channels limited to inbox|push|email|os, quiet hours with IANA timezone and HH:MM start/end.
Defaults per CT-NOTIF-PAYLOAD (approval_needed -> inbox+push+os; billing_issue -> inbox+email; everything else inbox) returned when the user never saved preferences.
Server-enforced invariants: security_alert and billing_issue always keep `inbox`; quiet hours can never suppress them.
Pure functions isQuietNow(prefs, now) (handles overnight ranges and DST via the timezone database) and the PreferencesPort implementation for B063.
ETag on GET and If-Match on PUT.
scope_out: Inbox API: B065. Dispatcher routing code: B063. Push registry: B064.
Email unsubscribe links/compliance footer (email service, B032).
build_against: Postgres container or in-memory repository, fixed clocks with explicit time zones (Europe/Berlin, America/New_York, Pacific/Auckland) in tests, Fastify inject.
interfaces: GET /v1/notification-preferences -> 200 {channels: Record<NotifCategory, ('inbox'|'push'|'email'|'os')[]>, quiet_hours: {enabled:boolean, start:'HH:MM', end:'HH:MM', timezone:string, allow_high_approval:boolean}} with ETag
Table notification_pref(user_id pk, doc jsonb, updated_at, version int)
acceptance: GET for a user with no row returns the contract defaults for all 14 categories, with quiet_hours.enabled=false.

PUT with an unknown category or channel 'sms' returns 422 with errors[].pointer such as '/channels/approval_needed/0'; unknown extra top-level fields are ignored on read per the robustness rule but not persisted.

PUT that removes `inbox` from billing_issue or security_alert is stored with `inbox` re-added and the response shows it; quiet hours never alter their delivery (test via isQuietNow + decideChannels contract in B063 fixture).
isQuietNow with start 22:00 end 07:00 Europe/Berlin returns true at 23:30 local, true at 06:59, false at 07:00, and handles a DST changeover day without throwing or being wrong by an hour.
start == end is rejected 422 (zero-length window) ; an invalid timezone string is rejected 422.
PUT with stale If-Match returns 412 `precondition_failed`; a successful PUT changes the ETag.
Document size limit 8 KiB enforced (413/422) and the endpoint is rate limited per CT-PAGE.
tests: prefs.quiet-hours.test.ts: overnight, DST, time zones, property test across random instants
prefs.defaults.test.ts: defaults match the contract table
guardrails: MUST keep security_alert and billing_issue deliverable regardless of user prefs (inbox always on).
MUST validate the time zone against the platform IANA database, never trusting client-provided offsets.
MUST NOT store anything beyond the preference document (no device names, no tokens).
Defaults MUST be code-level constants tested against the contract, not rows seeded in the DB.
failure_modes: Stored document fails validation after a code change (stale shape) -> service returns defaults merged with valid parts and logs a warning, never a 500.
Concurrent PUTs -> last write wins unless If-Match given; version increments atomically.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: the preference document shape (channels x categories, quiet hours fields) is described only in prose in CT-API-NOTIFY; the shape above is this lane's proposal pending openapi.yaml. 'High may bypass quiet hours only for approval_needed if the user opted in' is modelled as quiet_hours.allow_high_approval.
